audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagreed between layers on all seven rows: full phases[].side read Viktor/Viktor/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Viktor while content win[] read Akali/Akali/Viktor/Viktor/Akali/Akali/Akali. The page rendered two different answers to 'who wins Level 1'.
audit.why: content win[] matches the packet levelChart exactly, and matches the kit reality: Viktor has no zoning tool until Gravity Field (W) at 3, and his strength window is 3-5 before Akali's level 6 execute. The full layer was the wrong copy.
audit.corrected: Full layer flipped to Akali/Akali/Viktor/Viktor/Akali/Akali/Akali, proposed as one atomic group; content layer already agrees so no content-side edits were needed. phases[2].why and phases[3].why rewritten so the prose no longer claims Akali wins those stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text named Viktor's ultimate 'Chaos Storm' and his E 'Death Ray' — both are pre-rework names.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon has R = Arcane Storm (120/100/80s) and E = Hextech Ray (12/11/10/9/8s, 525 range). Viktor's real lane spike is Gravity Field at 3 plus Hextech Ray ranks; Akali's counter-spikes are Perfect Execution at 6 and first item.
audit.corrected: All four spikes and the mid/late prose now use Hextech Ray and Arcane Storm, with the 9s Hextech Ray cooldown made concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing stated the decisive interactions: Twilight Shroud does not stop Gravity Field or Hextech Ray, Siphon Power shields through Akali's burst, and Siphon Power opens with an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Shroud makes Akali untargetable, but Gravity Field is a ground zone and Hextech Ray is a line skillshot — both still damage and stun her inside the smoke, which is the single most common way this lane is lost. Siphon Power (9s at rank 1) grants a shield and empowers his next attack, so his wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries the real numbers and the shroud caveat; the auto-reset tell is recorded in notes for the trading fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gave no numbers and repeated the same sentence twice.
audit.why: Gravity Field 17/16/15/14/13s and Hextech Ray 12/11/10/9/8s are the two windows the lane runs on.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with per-rank cooldowns and the commit condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: enemyWin and breakdown.carry were structural templates — the same sentence with a name swapped in.
audit.why: Template sweep: 'wins by landing X, denying your pattern' and 'Carry through deletions — one carry per fight' paste onto any enemy.
audit.corrected: Both regrounded in Viktor's actual kit.

edits.before: Shroud online: the trade pattern is Q-auto, shroud the answer, Q again from the smoke. Most mids lose this exchange.
edits.after: Shroud online, but Gravity Field zones the smoke — the stun still lands inside it and Hextech Ray chips you off the wave.

edits.before: Passive-weave every trade: spell, walk out of the ring, auto the edge — the energy refunds pay the whole lane.
edits.after: Hextech Ray is down to 9s here and Siphon Power shields his chip back — cross Gravity Field, never stand in it.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Check it before every step-up. - W Twilight Shroud is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Gravity Field: 17s at rank 1, 13s maxed — it only stuns if you linger, so cross it and never sit in it. - Hextech Ray: 9s by rank 4, 525 range, and it still hits you inside the shroud. - Siphon Power shields on a 9s clock — burst after it pops, not into it.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Viktor wins by stunning you inside Gravity Field, shielding through your burst with Siphon Power, and chipping you out at 525.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — one carry per fight, every fight; the shroud buys the time and the resets pay the exit.
edits.after: Viktor is the deletion — R past Gravity Field, shroud his Hextech Ray, take the reset out. No Viktor, no zone on the fight.

edits.before: Viktor's Death Ray poke and augmented zone control at levels 4-5 out-trade your engage attempts during this stretch.
edits.after: Viktor's Hextech Ray poke on a 9s clock and Gravity Field zoning out-trade your engage attempts through levels 4-5.

edits.before: Your burst-and-reset combo swings level 6 back in your favor by killing him before Chaos Storm's damage fully ticks.
edits.after: Your burst-and-reset combo swings level 6 back in your favor by killing him before Arcane Storm's damage fully ticks.

edits.before: You still win the all-in through levels 1-2 by dashing in on his slow autos, but once he finishes Hex Core upgrades around 3-5 his Gravity Field zoning and Death Ray poke start winning straight trades.
edits.after: You still win the all-in through levels 1-2 by dashing in on his slow autos, but from level 3 his Gravity Field zoning and Hextech Ray poke start winning straight trades — and neither one is stopped by your shroud.

edits.before: Your Perfect Execution reset comes back online at level 6 and lets you burst him down before Chaos Storm's follow-up damage ticks fully, flipping the lane back your way.
edits.after: Perfect Execution arrives at level 6 and lets you burst him down before Arcane Storm's follow-up ticks, but open after Siphon Power pops or the shield eats the combo.

edits.before: A Rocketbelt or Riftmaker reset lets you dash through his Gravity Field zone twice, closing the distance he relies on to kite with Death Ray.
edits.after: A Riftmaker or Stormsurge spike lets you cross Gravity Field and re-enter on the E reset, closing the range he relies on to kite with Hextech Ray.

edits.before: Late your reset burst still one-shots him if you land it clean, but you must dodge his Chaos Storm zone entirely since standing in it for even a second lets his team clean you up.
edits.after: Late your reset burst still one-shots him if you land it clean, but you must leave his Arcane Storm zone entirely — he redirects it, so walking out once is not the same as being clear.

edits.before: Once his Hex Core evolves around levels 3-5, Gravity Field zoning and Death Ray poke make it genuinely hard to close distance, and this is the one stretch of the lane where he out-trades you at range.
edits.after: From level 3 to 5, Gravity Field zoning and Hextech Ray poke make it genuinely hard to close distance, and this is the one stretch where he out-trades you — the shroud hides you but does not stop either spell.

edits.before: Your combo returns to favor at level 6 and beyond since Perfect Execution outburns his ramping poke, but you must dash in through or around Chaos Storm rather than committing while standing in its damage zone.
edits.after: Your combo returns to favor at level 6 since Perfect Execution outburns his ramping poke, but dash through or around Arcane Storm rather than committing inside it — he steers the storm onto you after you land.

edits.before: Zone with Gravity Field and Death Ray to keep you outside dash range through mid game
edits.after: Zone with Gravity Field and Hextech Ray to keep you outside your 825 E range

edits.before: Use Chaos Storm defensively to peel and slow you the instant you commit
edits.after: Use Arcane Storm defensively and redirect it onto you the instant you commit

edits.before: All-in immediately off cooldown once his Chaos Storm is used defensively, not offensively
edits.after: All-in the moment Gravity Field is spent and Siphon Power's shield has already popped

notes: Level chart was split across layers on all 7 rows; content matched the packet so only the full layer was flipped, as one atomic group. Two stale ability names corrected throughout: Death Ray -> Hextech Ray, Chaos Storm -> Arcane Storm. Packet suspectNames flagged 'Your Perfect Execution' as a near-miss — that is a FALSE POSITIVE, Perfect Execution is Akali's real R name and the capital Y is just sentence start. Derived-flag conflict: Viktor's R carries the 'channel: interruptible' flag, but Riot's own text says the storm interrupts ENEMY channels and can be redirected — it does not say Viktor is channelling. Per the rule I trusted the description and made no claim that CC cancels his ult. Unverified and therefore not written: whether Twilight Shroud's untargetability drops an already-travelling Hextech Ray, whether Gravity Field's stun ticks accumulate while Akali is invisible inside it, and whether Akali's R recast can be buffered through the Gravity Field stun. The missingInteractions auto-reset tell (Siphon Power empowers his next attack, so the wind-up is the cue) is reflected in the new breakdown.cooldowns line rather than tradeGood, which was already grounded and inside its length band.
